title: File indirection escapes a closed runtime trust root

scenario.observed_change: Runtime-image normalization accepts file indirection that may resolve outside the attested runtime root, allowing external bytes to enter an image intended to have a closed trusted inventory.
controlled_inputs: file indirection targets outside the runtime root
mutable_state: effective target of an indirect file entry
authority_boundaries: attested runtime root versus external filesystem content
logical in-root file name versus effective resolved file
operation_model: accept an indirect file entry as part of normalization
resolve/read the effective target outside the runtime root
copy external bytes into the normalized trusted image

required_invariants.requirement: Containment and trusted identity must apply to the effective resource used by the operation after indirection, not only to the original logical path.
Lower-trust external bytes must not cross into a privileged/trusted artifact without the required validation boundary.

must_investigate: whether containment is enforced on the resolved resource
whether any external-file exception is narrowly identity-bound
must_identify: closed-root trust can be bypassed when a logical in-root entry resolves to arbitrary external bytes
must_not_claim: closed trusted inventory solely because the logical entry name is inside the runtime root

provenance.note: GitHub Copilot review identified that file indirection could resolve outside the runtime cache root and import arbitrary external bytes into the normalized trusted image.
